description: We’re Ctrl Alt Orbit, a team from Thrissur taking on the Space Mission Design Game challenge. We’re building a web-based game where players plan a space mission by choosing a destination, designing a spacecraft, and managing budget, fuel, and crew, with code-breaking puzzles along the way. We enjoy coding, problem-solving, and space exploration.
summary:
MISSION X is a browser-based educational game that lets anyone experience the trade-offs behind real spacecraft design. Instead of only reading about budgets, mass limits and power requirements, players make engineering decisions and immediately see the consequences.

THE PROBLEM
Space missions depend on many connected decisions. A bigger science payload adds value but also adds mass, needs more power and may require a larger rocket, which costs more. Students and beginners rarely get a hands-on way to see how these choices affect one another, so space engineering can feel abstract and out of reach.

details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

MISSION X is a browser-based game in which the player designs a spacecraft for a Moon, Mars or Deep Space mission. The player picks a launch vehicle, a science payload, a power system and a communication system within a fictional budget. Live telemetry shows cost, spacecraft mass, rocket payload capacity, power supply versus demand and communication reliability, with warnings before launch. The player then runs the mission: an animated countdown and flight to the destination leads to a mission report with a score out of 100, a 1–3 star rating and a debrief explaining which choices helped or hurt. Players can redesign and try again, and the game saves their personal best and last five attempts for each level.

BENEFITS

Players learn by doing. In a few minutes they discover that payload mass must fit rocket capacity, power must meet instrument demand, reliable communication improves safety, and spare margin protects a mission from surprises. Failing is safe and instant, so experimenting is encouraged. The game needs no install, account or server and works on laptops and phones, so classrooms and home learners can use it easily.
